title: Existentialism is a later label, not a membership roll
summary: Kevin Aho's Stanford entry is the overview. Several famous names rejected or predate the label.
body: Kevin Aho's Stanford Encyclopedia entry on existentialism is the overview used here. The v1 article lists Kierkegaard, Nietzsche, Sartre, Camus, and Beauvoir as existentialists and quotes "existence precedes essence" and "condemned to be free." Those phrases are associated with Sartre's 1946 lecture. The SEP Sartre entry (Jack Reynolds and Pierre-Jean Renaudie) says that lecture offered an accessible version of Being and Nothingness (1943). Short copyrighted sentences are not copied. Kierkegaard and Nietzsche wrote before the twentieth-century label. Camus separated himself from it. The v1 roll is a later classification, useful and disputed.
said_by: Kevin Aho; Jack Reynolds and Pierre-Jean Renaudie
